title: The Napkin and the Sidechain: from a Commodore in Houston to the Bitcoin Embassy on Reconquista
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Buenos Aires, a birth date the record will not confirm
stops.date_confidence: One institutional publication of candidate members gives 28 January 1975. No primary civil record was reached, and the Consejo Profesional de Ciencias Económicas CV page, fetched directly for this research, carries his full career history and no birth date at all. Birthplace not established; pinned to the Buenos Aires city centroid by convention.
stops.campa: A boy is born into an Argentina whose currency will be renamed four times before he is twenty. The date given for him is the twenty-eighth of January, 1975, the year of the Rodrigazo, when prices in Buenos Aires double in a season and the state's own accountants stop trusting their arithmetic. His early life survives as a list of companies: the professional register that later prints his working life gives Clarín, Patagon, ElSitio, Edunexo, every employer and no birthday. Nothing reachable names the hospital, the neighborhood, or the parents.
suggested_refs: Curriculum vitae page for Diego Gutiérrez Zaldívar, archivo.consejo.org.ar/Cvs/zaldivar_diego.html
sources: dossier-cited candidate-member publication for the 1975-01-28 figure

stops.name: Palermo Norte, the Escuela Adolfo Van Gelderen
stops.date_confidence: The enrollment years 1982-1987 come from iq.wiki, a user-editable wiki, and rest on no school record reached here; month and day default to 01. The school is independently locatable: OpenStreetMap has Escuela Primaria Común 26 Adolfo Van Gelderen at Jerónimo Salguero 2455, which corrects the dossier's coordinate by about two kilometers.
stops.campa: He enters primary school at Jerónimo Salguero 2455 in the year the junta sends conscripts to the Malvinas, and leaves it in 1987, four years into the restored republic. The building is an ordinary Buenos Aires common school, Escuela N. 26, named for Adolfo Van Gelderen. What survives of the boy in this period is not the school but a machine he is given in another country. No teacher, no report card, no classmate has surfaced from those six years, and the only source for his being there at all is a wiki anyone may edit.
suggested_refs: OpenStreetMap feature 'Escuela Primaria Común 26 Adolfo Van Gelderen', Jerónimo Salguero 2455, Palermo Norte

stops.name: Houston, the diploma and the Commodore
stops.date_confidence: iproup dates the episode only by his age, eleven, which places it around 1985 or 1986; month and day default to 01. The coordinate is the Houston municipal point, 0.27 km from the OpenStreetMap city node.
stops.campa: In Houston his stepmother enrolls him, eleven years old, in a computer course built for adults. Nobody in the room is teaching children. The dossier that first told this story added a cousin who began the course beside him and dropped out; that cousin appears in no source reached here. He finishes it anyway and takes the certificate. The diploma is in his own words thirty-five years later, and so is what came of it: his uncle answers the certificate with a machine, a Commodore, the first computer he owns, carried home to Buenos Aires.
stops.quote: obtuve el diploma. Mi tío me regaló la primera computadora que era una Commodore
stops.quote_source: Diego Gutiérrez Zaldívar, iproup.com, 'El otro Diego argentino que llegó al Crypto Hall of Fame', 8 June 2021
suggested_refs: iproup.com, 'El otro Diego argentino que llegó al Crypto Hall of Fame', 8 June 2021

stops.name: San Nicolás, the Instituto Libre de Segunda Enseñanza
stops.date_confidence: The 1988-1992 span and the humanistic bachillerato come from iq.wiki alone; no registrar's record was reached, and month and day default to 01. The address is corrected: ILSE stands on Libertad in San Nicolás, not at the Recoleta address the dossier carried, which Nominatim resolves only to a street in Los Polvorines, twenty-nine kilometers outside the city.
stops.campa: He takes his secondary years at the Instituto Libre de Segunda Enseñanza, the University of Buenos Aires preparatory school, in a humanistic bachillerato rather than a technical one. He leaves in 1992, and no registrar's record of any of it was reached. The middle of that span is 1989: hyperinflation past three thousand percent, supermarkets looted, a president leaving office five months early. A boy who already owns a computer studies Latin and literature while the currency around him stops meaning anything for the second time in his short life.
suggested_refs: OpenStreetMap feature 'Instituto Libre de Segunda Enseñanza', Libertad, San Nicolás

stops.name: Paseo Colón 850, the engineering degree he does not finish
stops.date_confidence: iq.wiki records the 1993 entry into electrical and electronic engineering and that the degree was never completed; no diploma, enrollment record, or leaving date was located. Month and day default to 01. The coordinate is corrected to the OpenStreetMap point for the faculty building, 0.67 km from the dossier's.
stops.campa: He enrolls at the Facultad de Ingeniería on Avenida Paseo Colón, in electrical and electronic engineering, in a country that has just pegged its peso one to one against the dollar and believes the inflation problem is solved forever. He does not finish. Public profiles agree on the abandonment and none of them supplies a year for it, a reason, or a last exam, and no Argentine faculty yet offers a degree in the thing he does next. Within two years he is on the founding team building the first web edition of a national newspaper.
suggested_refs: Facultad de Ingeniería, Universidad de Buenos Aires, Avenida Paseo Colón 850

stops.name: Piedras 1743, the newspaper learns to be a website
stops.date_confidence: iproup has him starting on the web edition in 1994 with a 1995 launch; iq.wiki records instead 'webmaster for Clarín newspaper (1995-1999)'. The two spans are left in contradiction. Month and day default to 01. The coordinate is corrected: the address point Piedras 1743 lies in Barracas, 1.3 km south of the dossier's pin.
stops.campa: He joins the founding team that puts Clarín on the web, in the years when a newspaper's first website is built by people who must first explain to the newsroom what a link is. The work includes early interactive columns and touchscreen interfaces, hardware that will not become ordinary for another fifteen years. Two sources disagree about how long he stays: one has him there for the 1994 build and the 1995 launch, the other keeps him as webmaster until 1999. Nobody has reconciled them.
suggested_refs: Clarín Digital, first web edition of the newspaper, launched 1995

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the founding team of Patagon.com
stops.date_confidence: Three spans disagree and are not adjudicated: Patagon.com was founded in 1997 by Wenceslao Casares and sold to Banco Santander in March 2000; iq.wiki dates his own involvement 1996-1998; the dossier carried 1998-2000. Month and day default to 01. The office coordinate is the dossier's and is not tied to a verified street address.
stops.campa: He is on the founding team of Patagon.com, the online financial community Wenceslao Casares builds out of Buenos Aires. He works beside the man who will later be called the person who brought bitcoin to Silicon Valley, more than a decade before either of them has heard the word. No cap table has surfaced, and no document reached here says what fraction of the sale, if any, reached him. Banco Santander Río buys the company in 2000 for a price the professional registers put at seven hundred and fifty million dollars.
suggested_refs: Patagon.com, sold to Banco Santander Río, March 2000

stops.name: Buenos Aires, twenty-five developers at ElSitio.com
stops.date_confidence: The professional-body CV, fetched directly, gives R&D Manager heading a twenty-five-person development team; iq.wiki calls him Head of R&D with no number, and the figure of twenty that the dossier also carried appears in no source reached here. The circa 1999-2001 span is inferred from the company's arc; month and day default to 01.
stops.campa: He runs research and development at ElSitio.com with twenty-five developers under him, at the top of the Latin American dot-com boom and just before it ends. That is the largest team he will command until the one he builds for a sidechain fifteen years later. The professional register he later files with the Consejo Profesional de Ciencias Económicas gives the number; the crowdsourced wiki gives only the title; a third figure of twenty, repeated in the dossier, comes from nowhere reachable.
suggested_refs: Consejo Profesional de Ciencias Económicas CV page, listing the ElSitio.com R&D role

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Xinergia and the first ADSL
stops.date_confidence: The Xinergia span of roughly seventeen years, and the Internet Argentina and Edunexo roles, come from corporate biographies attached to RSK, RIF and Bitcoin Argentina founding-team materials. No incorporation record, contract, or filing was located for any of the three. The 2002 date orders the segment rather than dating a founding.
stops.campa: For roughly seventeen years he runs Xinergia, a web-development firm of his own, while his name attaches to two further ventures the corporate biographies repeat without documents: Internet Argentina, an early provider credited with the country's first ADSL service, and Edunexo, a system for administering schools and universities across Latin America and Spain. Seventeen years of a working life rest on biographies its subjects supplied. No incorporation record for any of the three was reached in this research.
suggested_refs: RSK, RIF and Bitcoin Argentina founding-team biographies enumerating Xinergia, Internet Argentina and Edunexo
sources: corporate founding-team biographies cited in the dossier, not independently verified

stops.name: The samba-technical list, a question from a CTO
stops.date_confidence: attested: the message is dated 1 September 2010 in the public list archive. The coordinate is the Buenos Aires centroid, standing for a message sent from no recorded place.
stops.campa: On the first of September, 2010, signing as CTO of Trusted Translations, he writes to a public mailing list of Samba developers to ask about migrating a Windows Server 2003 domain onto a Samba 4 development build. It is a technical question about somebody else's protocol, asked plainly, with no biographer standing between him and the record. The message is still in the archive, threaded, headers intact, one of the very few traces he left himself of his working life before bitcoin.
suggested_refs: samba-technical mailing list archive, message of 1 September 2010, lists.samba.org/archive/samba-technical/2010-September/073066.html

stops.name: Buenos Aires, a friend from Silicon Valley
stops.date_confidence: His own retrospective, iproup, 8 June 2021, dates this to 2012 and credits an unnamed Silicon Valley friend. Later biographical profiles instead credit Wenceslao Casares and date the introduction to 2011. The two accounts are left in contradiction, and the fifteen days of reading and the mining purchase carried by the dossier are in neither. Month and day default to 01.
stops.campa: A friend back from Silicon Valley tells him about bitcoin and then does the more persuasive thing: deposits him the equivalent of fifty thousand dollars in it. He is thirty-seven, has watched the peso renamed, hyperinflated, pegged and defaulted, and lives in a city where buying foreign currency has just been made nearly impossible. So he reads. Later profiles put this moment a year earlier and give the friend a name, Wenceslao Casares, whose company he had helped found fifteen years before. His own telling names nobody.
stops.quote: En el 2012, vino un amigo y me dijo: esto es espectacular
suggested_refs: iproup.com, 'El otro Diego argentino que llegó al Crypto Hall of Fame', 8 June 2021
sources: biographical profiles reproducing the Casares attribution, not independently corroborated

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the cepo cambiario and the dólar blue
stops.date_confidence: The exchange controls were imposed from late October 2011 and tightened through 2012; this 2012-01-01 pin matches the dated cepo cambiario stop already fixed at the same coordinate on Cristina Fernández de Kirchner's own file. Month and day default to 01.
stops.campa: The government of Cristina Fernández de Kirchner closes the door on the dollar: purchases require approval, approval is refused, and a parallel rate opens in the street within weeks. Argentines call it the dólar blue and pay it. In cafés and fast-food outlets across the city, buyers and sellers of bitcoin begin meeting to trade cash for a currency no ministry can ration, coordinating through LocalBitcoins, Facebook groups and Meetup. Nathaniel Popper will come in 2015 to write the scene up for the New York Times Magazine.
suggested_refs: Nathaniel Popper, 'Can Bitcoin Conquer Argentina?', The New York Times Magazine, 29 April 2015
sources: Nathaniel Popper, NYT Magazine, 29 April 2015 (PDF fetched and parsed directly)

stops.name: Palermo, the meetup in the McDonald's
stops.date_confidence: He dates the first organized meetup to 2012; the dossier carried 2011. Month and day are set to order the segment and are not attested. The coordinate is the Palermo pin the dossier uses for both this and the later La Maquinita fair.
stops.campa: He takes over the running of a small standing meetup and holds it wherever people will sit: cafés, and a McDonald's, with a laptop and a phone and cash changing hands across the table. The number of people is small enough that everyone who will build the Argentine bitcoin world for the next decade fits around a few tables in Palermo, and none of them is paid for it. Rodolfo Andragnes comes to one of these and stays. Franco Amati, named in the founding documents a year later, is not in his own account of the room.
stops.quote: Me juntaba en cafeterías, en Mc Donald
suggested_refs: Nathaniel Popper, 'Can Bitcoin Conquer Argentina?', on the cash-trading café scene of 2012-2013
sources: Nathaniel Popper, NYT Magazine, 29 April 2015 (PDF fetched directly)

stops.name: La Maquinita, Palermo Soho: the first fair
stops.date_confidence: The El Cronista / Information Technology piece is dated 29 October 2013; it was not independently re-fetched in this pass, and the account rests on the dossier's citation of it.
stops.campa: The meetups outgrow the tables. At La Maquinita, a coworking space in Palermo Soho, the group holds what the press calls the first organized Argentine bitcoin fair. The organizer Francisco Dosca explains to a reporter that they had been managing one or two informal gatherings a month and wanted to scale up. Six weeks later the same nucleus will fill a hotel in the financial district with people flown in from four continents. Nothing in the record explains how they got from the one to the other that fast.
suggested_refs: El Cronista / Information Technology, 'La experiencia Bitcoin en la Argentina desde adentro', 29 October 2013

stops.name: Buenos Aires, ONG Bitcoin Argentina is founded
stops.date_confidence: bitcoin.ar's own Nosotros page, fetched directly, dates the founding to 2013 and names the three founding partners; no month or day is given and both default to 01, which places this stop before the October fair and the December conference by convention rather than by attestation.
stops.campa: Rodolfo Andragnes, Franco Amati and Diego Gutiérrez Zaldívar constitute an organization for a currency that has no office, no issuer, and no legal standing in Argentina. He becomes its first president. Its stated purpose is education: teaching a country with a long memory of confiscated savings what a protocol is and how to hold one. Andragnes takes the conference and the public face, Amati the technical and activist side. The three names are still on the founding roster thirteen years later, on the organization's own page.
suggested_refs: ONG Bitcoin Argentina, 'Nosotros', bitcoin.ar

stops.name: Hotel Meliá, Reconquista 945: the first LaBitConf
stops.date_confidence: attested: the conference ran 7-8 December 2013 at the Hotel Meliá. The attendance figure of roughly four hundred and the thirty-plus exhibitors carried by the dossier are unverified; the conference's own archived site advertises 'over 25 International Speakers' and no attendance or exhibitor count at all, and the dossier's '18 December 2013 or thereabouts' is simply wrong.
stops.campa: The first Latin American Bitcoin Conference opens in a hotel three blocks from the Buenos Aires stock exchange, in a country where the central bank has not yet said the word in public. It runs two days, the seventh and eighth of December, in the financial district of a city under capital controls. Wenceslao Casares is on the speaker list. So are Andreas Antonopoulos, Anthony Di Iorio and Nicolás Cary, who go home and call it the best conference of the year, a verdict that puts Buenos Aires on the map of an industry two years old.
suggested_refs: Archived labitconf.com speakers page for the December 2013 edition
Cointelegraph, 'LaBITconf Rio 2014', quoting the organizers on the 2013 edition
sources: Cointelegraph, 'LaBITconf Rio 2014: First World-Class Bitcoin Conference in Brazil' (fetched directly)

stops.name: Marcelo T. de Alvear 405, the Bitcoin Embassy
stops.date_confidence: attested for the building and its specifications, El Cronista, 16 June 2014, by Verónica Dalto. That article names neither Gutiérrez Zaldívar nor Franco Amati anywhere in the piece and does not describe three floors; Amati as the space's cofounder and host, and Gutiérrez Zaldívar and the foundation as its impellers, rest on the dossier alone and are unattested here. The coordinate sits 0.12 km from the OpenStreetMap address point.
stops.campa: Five hundred square meters at the corner of Reconquista and Marcelo T. de Alvear, in the middle of the financial district: seven offices, a training room for fifty, coworking desks for twenty-four, one meeting room, one triple bedroom, a rooftop terrace. They call it the Bitcoin Embassy. The newspaper that describes the building does not mention Gutiérrez Zaldívar once. Andragnes, speaking as vice president of the association, describes a passport that would let anyone working in one such embassy walk into any other in the world.
stops.quote: Un programa que queremos desarrollar entre las distintas embajadas es el pasaporte, de manera que quienes trabajan en una embajada tengan acceso libre a las demás en el mundo.
stops.quote_source: Rodolfo Andragnes, vice president of the association, in El Cronista, 'Nada virtual: la Embajada Bitcoin llega a la Argentina y se instala en plena City', 16 June 2014
suggested_refs: El Cronista, 'Nada virtual: la Embajada Bitcoin llega a la Argentina', 16 June 2014
sources: OpenStreetMap address point, Marcelo T. de Alvear 405

stops.name: Copacabana, the conference leaves Argentina
stops.date_confidence: The 6-7 December 2014 dates and the speaker list are attested in Cointelegraph's account. The Rio Othon Palace as venue is not named in that article and remains unverified; the coordinate is the hotel's address point on Avenida Atlântica, 0.57 km from the dossier's.
stops.campa: The second LaBitConf is held in Rio de Janeiro, a year after the first, and the Buenos Aires edition is already the benchmark the organizers measure it against. Jeff Garzik, Tony Gallippi, Nicolás Cary, Anthony Di Iorio and Juan Llanos speak, alongside a Brazilian bench nobody in Argentina had heard of a year earlier. The conference has begun to do what it was designed to do, which is to exist without its founders in the room. He and Andragnes built the thing and are not named once in the surviving coverage of this edition.
suggested_refs: Cointelegraph, 'LaBITconf Rio 2014: First World-Class Bitcoin Conference in Brazil'

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the napkin and the whitepaper
stops.date_confidence: The founding year 2015 and the two-person core, Gutiérrez Zaldívar as chief executive and Sergio Demián Lerner as chief scientist, are attested in FinSMEs, 28 March 2016. The fuller enumeration adding Gabriel Kurman, Adrián Eidelman and Rubén Altman appears in no source reached here and stays a reconstruction. Month and day default to 01; the napkin is his own retelling, given ten years afterward.
stops.campa: With Sergio Demián Lerner, the cryptographer who found the Patoshi pattern in the earliest blocks and disclosed vulnerabilities in Bitcoin Core, he founds RSK Labs. The idea is a sidechain: a second network pegged to bitcoin, running the smart contracts bitcoin itself refuses to run. He is chief executive, Lerner chief scientist. He will tell the story ten years later as a napkin in Buenos Aires that became a whitepaper. Three other names appear in later enumerations of the founding team, and in none of the sources reached here.
stops.quote: Rootstock comenzó como una idea escrita en una servilleta en Buenos Aires, que se convirtió en el Whitepaper de Rootstock, publicado exactamente hace diez años.
stops.quote_source: Diego Gutiérrez Zaldívar, quoted in Cointelegraph en español, 21 November 2025
suggested_refs: The Rootstock (RSK) whitepaper, 2015
QUEUE.md row 23, Sergio Demián Lerner, queued and unresearched

stops.name: Colonia Juárez, LaBitConf in Mexico City
stops.date_confidence: The 4-5 December 2015 dates and the venue, EBC Campus Dinamarca, are attested on the conference's own site as captured 4 December 2015. The coordinate is an approximation for that campus in Colonia Juárez and is not an OpenStreetMap-verified point; the generic pin the dossier carried is the Zócalo, about 2.5 km away, and is wrong for this venue.
stops.campa: The conference moves north for its third edition, to a business school campus in Colonia Juárez: forty speakers, three hundred seats, two days. The model he and Andragnes designed in Buenos Aires is now itinerant, arriving in a capital, gathering whoever in that country is already doing this quietly, and leaving a local scene behind it when it goes. The rotation is less orderly than the retrospectives make it: the archived site records an edition the dossier skipped entirely, back in Buenos Aires on 4 and 5 November 2016.
suggested_refs: Archived labitconf.com capture of 4 December 2015, Mexico DF edition

stops.name: Buenos Aires, a million dollars for the sidechain
stops.date_confidence: attested: FinSMEs, 28 March 2016, fetched successfully in this pass, reports the completed one-million-dollar seed round led by Bitmain Technology, Coinsilium and Digital Currency Group. The earlier tranche of roughly one hundred thousand dollars from Coinsilium in January 2016, and the roughly three hundred and fifty thousand dollar opening round, appear in no source reached here and remain reconstruction.
stops.campa: RSK Labs closes a seed round of a million dollars on the twenty-eighth of March, 2016, led by Bitmain, the largest manufacturer of bitcoin mining hardware in the world, by the London-listed investor Coinsilium, and by Digital Currency Group, the New York fund that owns Grayscale. Four years earlier he was counting cash across a table in a Palermo McDonald's. The company is fifteen months old and has shipped no network. What it has is a whitepaper and a cryptographer with a reputation.
suggested_refs: FinSMEs, 'RSK Labs Raises $1M', 28 March 2016

stops.name: Reconquista 266, the central bank opens a door
stops.date_confidence: The dossier cites a BCRA hackathon program archive listing a talk of his titled 'La revolución Bitcoin' and dates it loosely to 2016 or 2017; the PDF was not re-rendered in this pass and no exact date was established. Month and day default to 01. The coordinate is the dossier's for the central bank and was not corrected against an address point.
stops.campa: The Banco Central de la República Argentina runs a financial-innovation hackathon and puts on its program a talk called La revolución Bitcoin, given by the president of a foundation for a currency the same institution's exchange controls had made useful four years earlier. National ministries appear on the same agenda, and the central bank and the bitcoin community talk to each other in public for a day. The program PDF is the only record of the event reached in this research. It gives a title and no date.
suggested_refs: BCRA hackathon program archive, bcra.gob.ar/archivos/Pdfs/Noticias/agenda_hackaton.pdf

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the mainnet opens in stages
stops.date_confidence: Corrected against the primary record. Retrospectives, the dossier included, give January 2018. Wayback captures of rsk.co carry no mainnet language on 4 December 2017 and the staged-opening text from the 6 December 2017 capture onward, still present on 9 January and 3 May 2018. The launch was staged and whitelisted, which is why the retrospectives disagree; 6 December 2017 is the first capture that carries it.
stops.campa: The network opens, and it opens carefully: projects must apply to be whitelisted before they can deploy on it. Somewhere between the fourth and the sixth of December, 2017, the company's homepage changes to say so, in the month bitcoin runs toward twenty thousand dollars and the word blockchain enters every boardroom on earth. Corporate retrospectives will place the launch in January of the following year; the captured pages say December. Two years and eleven months after the napkin, the sidechain is carrying transactions.
stops.quote: We always put security first at RSK. Therefore, we are opening our MainNet Network in a staged approach.
stops.quote_source: rsk.co homepage, Wayback capture of 6 December 2017
suggested_refs: Wayback Machine captures of rsk.co, 4 December 2017 through 3 May 2018
sources: web.archive.org captures of rsk.co (walked directly in this pass)
Cambridge Centre for Alternative Finance, 'Cryptoasset Ecosystem in Latin America and the Caribbean' (2023), dossier-cited, not re-rendered

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the TEDxRíodelaPlata stage
stops.date_confidence: The talk is attested on TED's own site; the dossier dates it to May 2019 and no day was established, so the day defaults to 01.
stops.campa: He walks onto the largest stage in Argentine public speaking and argues that a blockchain can carry reputation, and that reputation carried well is the basis on which strangers cooperate at planetary scale. Then he states the other half plainly: the same digital identity can free people the banks have never served, or hand an authority a more complete record of a life than any state has held. He does not resolve it on stage. The talk is titled Tu identidad, reputación y confianza en blockchain.
suggested_refs: TED, 'Diego Gutiérrez Zaldívar: Tu identidad, reputación y confianza en blockchain'

stops.name: Buenos Aires, IOV Labs buys Taringa!
stops.date_confidence: attested: Criptonoticias, 27 September 2019, fetched directly, with the Spanish quotation and Matías Botbol staying on. The English sentence 'This acquisition puts us at the forefront of distributed ledger adoption', carried by the dossier as verbatim, is not in that article. Taringa's inactivity by 2024 is carried from the dossier's framing and was not re-verified with a shutdown notice.
stops.campa: IOV Labs buys Taringa!, the Argentine social network of more than thirty million registered users and about a thousand active communities, the closest thing the Spanish-speaking internet had to a national commons. The plan is to pay users for what they post, in bitcoin, over Rootstock. Matías Botbol stays on as chief executive. Nobody alleges fraud, and no shutdown notice was located. By 2024 the platform is inactive and the decentralized economy it was bought to demonstrate has not arrived.
stops.quote: Blockchain es una tecnología poderosa, pero es necesaria la adopción masiva para crear un valor significativo
stops.quote_source: Diego Gutiérrez Zaldívar, CEO of IOVLabs, in Criptonoticias, 'Startup argentina RSK adquiere red social Taringa!', 27 September 2019
suggested_refs: Criptonoticias, 'Startup argentina RSK adquiere red social Taringa!', 27 September 2019

stops.name: Montevideo, the conference crosses the river
stops.date_confidence: attested: Montevideo.com.uy reports the 12-13 December 2019 dates in advance of the event. The attendance figures are the organizers' projections rather than a count.
stops.campa: LaBitConf is held in Uruguay for the first time. The organizers expect seven hundred people from more than twenty-five countries and over eighty speakers, and this is the last edition anyone will attend in a room for two years. The city is an hour by boat from the one where the thing started, and the crossing is the shortest journey the conference has ever made. Six years after the hotel on Reconquista, its founders no longer have to explain what it is for. The attendance figures are projections, not a count.
suggested_refs: Montevideo.com.uy, 'Labitconf se realizará por primera vez en Uruguay el 12 y 13 de diciembre'

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the conference goes to the moon
stops.date_confidence: Corrected: the dossier gave a single-day virtual edition named 'La Luna'. The archived labitconf.com of 2 December 2020 brands it labitmoon and dates it 7 to 12 December 2020, a five-day hybrid run of live streams and roundtables with 3D motion capture content.
stops.campa: With the borders shut and the country under one of the longest lockdowns in the world, the conference runs for five days as a digital experience called labitmoon: live streams, roundtables, content shot with motion capture, and a party in virtual reality on the lunar surface. The brand does not miss a year. It has now run continuously since the Hotel Meliá, through a pandemic, out of a city where nobody may leave the apartment after dark. The archived site dates the run from the seventh to the twelfth of December, 2020.
stops.quote: a VR Party on the Moon
suggested_refs: Archived labitconf.com capture of 2 December 2020, the labitmoon edition

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the interview with lavaca
stops.date_confidence: attested: Claudia Acuña's interview, lavaca.org, 21 May 2021, verified verbatim on several quotations. One correction to the dossier: the article does not end where it said. It continues past his remarks on bitcoin into Acuña's account of domestic-violence allegations against him and closes on his own responses to those, which is a different shape of piece from the one the dossier described.
stops.campa: He sits with a cooperative newsroom that has spent twenty years covering worker-recovered factories, and gives them the most political version of his argument he has given anyone: that what failed in Argentina was always the intermediary, that the corralito of 2001 would have been survivable with this tool, that the problem in politics is not ideology or values but that systems of concentrated power corrupt whoever holds them. He also tells them bitcoin has no intrinsic value. The piece does not end where he stops talking about bitcoin.
stops.quote: Otra hubiera sido la Historia si en 2001 hubiésemos tenido esta herramienta
stops.quote_source: Diego Gutiérrez Zaldívar to Claudia Acuña, 'Esta no es una nota sobre Bitcoin', lavaca.org, 21 May 2021
suggested_refs: Claudia Acuña, 'Esta no es una nota sobre Bitcoin', lavaca.org, 21 May 2021

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the other Diego
stops.date_confidence: The induction is reported by iproup on 8 June 2021, which is the article's date and not necessarily the ceremony's; the dossier's own citation was not otherwise corroborated. The honor is a curated private initiative under the Moonstock and Hyperbitcoinizer brand, not an industry-wide award, and the curator is named as Aaron Koenig.
stops.campa: The Argentine press announces that he is the first Latin American inducted into a Crypto Hall of Fame, and reaches for the only comparison the country's readers require, calling him the other Argentine Diego. He has by now spent nine years explaining this technology to Argentina, and the country files him under a name it already had.
